title: Rename notes column and cursor-paginate saved recipes
context: Repo: pantry-web, a consumer meal-planning web app on Postgres. user_recipes has ~140M rows and the heaviest users have more than 200k saved recipes; notes are user-written free text that users cannot recover elsewhere. Migrations run automatically on deploy after merge to main. API p99 budget is 300ms.

defects.description: Description calls this a pure rename with no data change, but the up migration adds an empty private_notes column and drops notes without copying data (should be RENAME COLUMN). Every user's notes are destroyed on deploy and the down migration cannot restore them.
defects.evidence: ALTER TABLE user_recipes DROP COLUMN notes;

defects.description: The query dropped LIMIT and now loads a user's entire saved list on every page request, slicing in memory; for users with 200k+ rows this blows the 300ms budget and memory on every scroll.
defects.evidence: ORDER BY ur.saved_at DESC, ur.id DESC`,

defects.description: If the cursor row no longer exists (recipe unsaved between pages), findIndex returns -1 so start becomes 0 and the client gets page one again, duplicating items and looping infinite scroll.

decoys: limit query param is clamped (Math.min(... || 50, 100)) so a client cannot request an unbounded page size.
private_notes is returned in the response, but this route is requireUser and filtered to the caller's own rows, so it is the owner reading their own notes.
